Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:10:1.hebrew: מחלוקת בשתי כיתי עדים - שאמר בעל דין בפנינו: "יש לי שתי כיתי עדים בדבר זה". הביא כת ראשונה, ועמד הלוה ואחר ואמר: "פסולין הן", דהשתא לאו כנוגע בעדות הוא, שהרי אמר מלוה שיש לו כת אחרת. ואם ביקש ולא מצא — יפסיד, דקסבר ר"מ: צריך בעל דין לברר ולהעמיד על האמת כל דבריו שטוען בבית דין, והני מיפסלי אף לעדיות אחרות. ואם ביקש ומצא כת אחרת כשירה, אף ע"פ שראשונה נפסלה — הרי בירר דבריו, שאמר להביאם והביא, והוא לא דק, דסבור שכשרים היו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:10:1.english: The dispute is with regard to two sets of witnesses - Where a litigant said before us [the court]: “I have two sets of witnesses in this matter.” He brought the first set, and the borrower and another [person] stood up and said: “They are disqualified,” for now he [the borrower] is not considered an interested party in the testimony, as the creditor said that he has another set [of witnesses]. And if [the creditor] sought and did not find [another set], he will lose [the case], as Rabbi Meir holds: A litigant must substantiate and establish the truth of all the statements that he claims in court; and these [first witnesses] are disqualified even for other testimonies. And if [the creditor] sought and found another, valid set, even though the first [set] was disqualified, he has substantiated his statements, for he said [he would] bring them and he brought [them], and he was [simply] not precise, since he assumed that they were valid.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:11:1.hebrew: ורבנן סברי אין צריך לברר - ויכול לומר: "אין לי עוד", ונמצא זה נוגע בעדותו הוא, ולא מיפסלי אפי' בעדות זו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:11:1.english: And the Rabbis hold that one is not required to substantiate - And [the litigant] can say: "I have no more [witnesses]," and consequently this [other litigant] has a personal interest in his testimony, and they are not disqualified even for this testimony.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:13:1.hebrew: נמצאת כת שניה קרובין או פסולין - ע"י עדים גמורים. מהו לר' מאיר? מי אמרינן: השתא ודאי נוגע בעדות הוא, דאין לחבירו כת אחרת כשרה; או דילמא: מעיקרא מיהת, כי אסהיד בעל דין ואחר עמו אקמאי למיפסלינהו, לאו נוגע בעדות הוא, דאכתי לא אשתכח כת שנייה פסולין? הכי גרסינן לה, כמו שפירשתי, ולא נהירא: חדא - דאין זה בירור דברים לר' מאיר, הואיל וכת האחת נפסלין, ועדיין נוגע בעדות הוא; ועוד - דאי נמי הוי בירור דברים בהכי, נוגע בעדות הוא, דאם לא ימצא כת אחרת כשרה אלא כת פסולה, נמצא מפסיד בפסול של ראשונים; דאי לא נפסלו ראשונים היה מוציא ממונו על פיהם ודבריו נבררין ע"י שניה, ואע"פ שפסולין, ועכשיו הוא מפסיד! הלכך אומר אני דגרסינן הכי, והוא עיקר: דר"מ סבר א"צ לברר, וזה שאמר להביא שתי כיתי עדים והביאם והאחת נפסלת - אין בכך כלום, שא"צ לברר דבריו ודיו בכת אחת הכשרין, ואלו נפסלין לעדות אחרת ע"פ בעל דין ואחר, דאינו נוגע בעדות; ורבנן סברי צריך לברר, ונמצא זה נוגע בעדות, ולא מפסיל. "נמצאת כת שניה קרובין או פסולין" לר' מאיר, מהו? נהי דא"צ לברר, מ"מ עכשיו אין כאן עדות, וה"ל נוגע בעדות למפרע; או דילמא: כי אסהיד מיהא לאו נוגע בעדות הוה, דאכתי לא מצאו כת שנייה פסולה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:13:1.english: If the second set was found to be relatives or disqualified - [Disqualified] by means of fully valid witnesses. What is [the halakha] according to Rabbi Meir? Do we say: Now he is certainly interested in the testimony, for his opponent has no other valid set [of witnesses]; or perhaps: Initially at least, when the litigant and another [witness] with him testified against the first [set] to disqualify them, he was not interested in the testimony, as the second set had not yet been found to be disqualified? This is the reading [of the Talmudic text] as I explained [above], but it does not appear correct: First, this does not constitute substantiation of [his] statements according to Rabbi Meir, since one of the sets is disqualified, and [the opposing litigant] is still interested in the testimony. And furthermore, even if this were considered a substantiation of [his] statements, in this [situation] he is interested in the testimony: for if [the first litigant] does not find another valid set, but rather [only] a disqualified set, he turns out to lose through the disqualification of the first [witnesses]; for had the first [witnesses] not been disqualified, he would have recovered his money based on their testimony, and his statement would have been substantiated through the second [set] even though they are disqualified, whereas now he loses! Therefore, I say that we should read the text as follows, and this is the primary [version]: "For Rabbi Meir holds: One does not need to substantiate [his statements]; and this [litigant] who said [he would] bring two sets of witnesses, and brought them, and one [set] was disqualified — that is of no consequence, as he does not need to substantiate his words, and it is sufficient for him with the one set that is valid; and these [disqualified witnesses] are disqualified for other testimony based on the litigant and another [witness with him], for he is not interested in the testimony. And the Rabbis hold: One must substantiate [his statements], and thus this [litigant] is found to be interested in the testimony, and [they] are not disqualified." [And as for the dilemma,] "If the second set was found to be relatives or disqualified" — according to Rabbi Meir, what is [the halakha]? Granted that he does not need to substantiate [his statements], nevertheless, now there is no testimony here at all, and he becomes interested in the testimony retroactively? Or perhaps: When he testified at any rate, he was not interested in the testimony, since they had not yet found the second set to be disqualified.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:14:1.hebrew: כבר העידו הראשונים - (כת ראשונה) כשנמצאת כת שניה פסולה, כבר נתקבלה בכשרות עדותן של אלו המעידין על הפסול, ועדיין לא היה נוגע בעדות, ומאחר שנתקבלה בהכשר — נאמנין לפסול את הראשונים. ל"א: כבר העידו העדים הראשונים — כת ראשונה שהעידו בעדותן של בעלי דינין, ומהימני; דכיון דשניה פסולה, תו לא מפסלי קמאי, דה"ל נוגע בעדות. ולשון ראשון נראה, מדנקט בהאי לישנא "כבר העידו":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:14:1.english: The first ones already testified - (The first set) When the second set is found to be disqualified, the testimony of these [witnesses] who testify to the disqualification has already been validly accepted, and at that time [the litigant] was not yet an interested party to the testimony; and since it was accepted validly, they are believed to disqualify the first ones. Another explanation: "The first witnesses already testified" — [meaning] the first set who testified in the testimony of the litigants, and they are believed; for since the second [set] is disqualified, the first ones can no longer be disqualified, as he is [now] an interested party to the testimony. And the first explanation appears [correct], since he used this phrasing: "They already testified."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:16:1.hebrew: הבא לידון בשטר ובחזקה - מחזיק בקרקע, ואמר לו חבירו: "מה לך בכאן?", וא"ל: "אתה מכרתיה לי, ואכלתיה שני חזקה, ועדיין שטר מכירה בידי". "נידון בשטר" — על כרחו צריך להביא השטר ויברר דבריו. ואם לא מצא שטר, יפסיד, דלא מהניא ליה חזקה. ואע"ג דחזקה במקום שטר קיימא, כדאמרי רבנן: "עד תלת שנין מזדהר איניש בשטרי', טפי לא מזדהר" — האי, כיון דאמר "ישנו בידי", צריך לברר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:16:1.english: One who comes to be judged with a deed and with presumptive ownership - [This refers to one who] is in possession of land, and his fellow said to him, "What [business] do you have here?" and he said to him, "You sold it to me, and I consumed [its produce for the] years of presumptive ownership, and the deed of sale is still in my possession." "[He] is judged by the deed" — against his will, he must bring the deed and substantiate his statements. And if he did not find [the] deed, he loses, for presumptive ownership does not avail him. And even though presumptive ownership stands in place of a deed, as the Sages said: "Up to three years a person is careful with his deed; more [than that] he is not careful" — this one, since he said "it is in my possession," must substantiate [his claim].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:16:2.hebrew: נידון בחזקה - משמע: על כרחו יביא עדי חזקה, ושטר לא מהני. להכי פריך: "בחזקה ולא בשטר?!", והא שטר עיקר ראיה הוא! וכיון דיש לו שטר, אין בחזקה אפי' משום בירור דברים, דבמקום שטר לא הוזכרה חזקה, דהיא גופא לא אתיא אלא מכח השטר, דאמר: "על ידי השטר החזקתי בו, ואבד ממני לאחר ג' שנים":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:16:2.english: Is judged on the basis of presumptive ownership - This implies that perforce he must bring witnesses of presumptive ownership, and a deed is of no avail. That is why [the Gemara] asks: “[On the basis of] presumptive ownership and not on the basis of a deed?!” For behold, a deed is the primary evidence; and since he has a deed, presumptive ownership does not even serve to clarify matters, for where there is a deed, presumptive ownership is not mentioned [at all], since [presumptive ownership] itself only derives from the power of a deed, for [the possessor] says: “By means of the deed I took possession of it, and it was lost from me after three years.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:17:1.hebrew: אף בחזקה - באיזה מהן שירצה. ואם יש לו עדי חזקה, א"צ לברר דבריו על השטר. והיינו דאמר ר' מאיר כרבי, ורבנן כר' שמעון:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:17:1.english: Even on the basis of presumptive ownership - By whichever of them he wishes; and if he has witnesses of presumptive ownership, he is not required to substantiate his claim regarding the deed. And that is [what the Gemara meant when it suggested that] Rabbi Meir [rules] in accordance with Rabbi, and the Rabbis in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:1:1.hebrew: ואמר רב דימי - הא דקתני "נאמן עלי אבא" — כגון דקבליה עליה בחד דיין, ויש שנים כשרין עמו. ואפילו הכי, כיון דפסול מדאורייתא, מצי הדר ביה. הכא נמי, כיון דחד לממון לא מתכשר, מצי הדר ביה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:1:1.english: And Rav Dimi says - That which [the mishna] teaches, “My father is trusted to me,” [is referring to a case] where he accepted him upon himself as one judge, and there are two fit [judges] with him. And even so, since he is disqualified by Torah law, he can retract. Here too, since a single [witness] is not qualified for monetary matters, he can retract.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:20:1.hebrew: <abbr title="אפילו">אפי'</abbr> תימא רבנן כרבי סבירא להו, דעד כאן לא קאמר רבי התם צריך לברר אלא משום דחזקה לאו עיקר ראיה הוא, דמכח השטר הוא דאתיא; דאי הוה טעין ברישא: החזקתי בה מעצמי שלא אמר לי אדם דבר מעולם — אין זו חזקה; וכי אמר לו: אתה מכרתיה לי, דהיינו בשטר, ואבדתיו לאחר <abbr title="שלוש">ג'</abbr> שנים — הויא חזקה. הלכך, האי, הואיל ואמר: ישנו בידי — צריך לברר. אבל אמר: יש לי <abbr title="שתי">ב'</abbr> כיתי <abbr title="עדים">עדי'</abbr>, והביא אחת — כיון דהני לאו מכח הני אתו, <abbr title="אין צריך">א"צ</abbr> לברר דבריו ולחזר אחר כת שניה. וללישנא בתרא <abbr title="הכי קאמר">ה"ק</abbr>: <abbr title="אפילו">אפי'</abbr> תימא תרווייהו אליבא דרבי פליגי, <abbr title="ורבי מאיר">ור"מ</abbr> אמר לך: אנא דאמר <abbr title="אפילו">אפי'</abbr> לרבי. ומשום דהלכה כרבי מחבריו, מהדרינן לאוקומא לפלוגתייהו אליביה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:20:1.english: Even if you say that the Rabbis hold in accordance with Rabbi, [the reasoning is] that Rabbi said there that one is required to substantiate [his claim] only because presumptive possession is not the primary proof, as it derives from the power of the deed; for if he had initially claimed, 'I held possession of it on my own, for no one ever said anything to me,' this is not a [valid] presumptive possession; and when he says to him, 'You sold it to me' — that is, by a deed — 'and I lost it after three years,' it is a [valid] presumptive possession. Therefore, this one, since he said, 'It is in my possession,' must substantiate [his words and produce it]. But if one said, 'I have two sets of witnesses,' and brought one [set], since these do not derive from the power of those, he is not required to substantiate his statement and search for the second set. And according to the latter version, this is what it means: Even if you say both of them disagree according to Rabbi, and Rabbi Meir [could] say to you: 'I say [my ruling] even according to Rabbi.' And because the halakhah follows Rabbi over his colleagues, we strive to establish their dispute according to his view.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:4:1.hebrew: אלמא דווקא קתני - מדשני במילתיה, דבדיינין נקט לשון יחיד ובעדים נקט לשון רבים, וליתא לדריש לקיש, והדרא קושיין לדוכתא: והא עדים כמומחין דמו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:4:1.english: Evidently, [the mishna] teaches [this] specifically - Since [the Tanna] varied his wording, as regarding judges he used the singular form and regarding witnesses he used the plural form, [the resolution of] Resh Lakish does not stand, and our objection returns to its place: But aren’t witnesses considered like expert [judges]?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:5:1.hebrew: א"ר אלעזר - סיפא, גבי עדים — בבא הוא ואחר לפוסלן, דהוו להו תרי דמסהדי אפסולה, ומהימני. ודיינין — בערכאות שבסוריא, כדאוקימנא; ולא פסול ממש קאמר, אלא: בעינא בי דינא מעליא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:5:1.english: Rabbi Elazar said - The latter clause [of the mishna], regarding witnesses, [is dealing with a case] where he and another [person] come to disqualify them, as they are two [witnesses] who testify about their disqualification, and they are believed. And [the clause regarding] judges [deals with] courts in Syria, as we established; and he does not mean an actual disqualification, but rather: "I want a superior court."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:6:1.hebrew: נוגע בעדותו הוא - האי בעל דין, דמשום דלא ליסהוד עליה קאתי למיפסליה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:6:1.english: He has a vested interest in his testimony - This litigant [is an interested party], for in order that [the witness] should not testify against him, he comes to disqualify him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:7:1.hebrew: שקרא עליו ערער - בעל דין אומר לפנינו על מה הוא פוסלו, ויש אחר עמו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:7:1.english: Where he raised a challenge against him - The litigant states before us on what grounds he disqualifies him, and there is another [person] with him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:7:2.english: A challenge - A taint of disqualification.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:8:1.hebrew: דגזלנותא - מעיד עליו הוא ואחר, שגזלן הוא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:8:1.english: Of robbery - He and another [witness] testify against him that he is a robber.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:8:2.english: He is an interested party in his testimony - He is saying [this] so that [the witness] will not testify against him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:9:1.hebrew: דפגם משפחה - עבד הוא, ממשפחת עבד שלא נשתחרר בא, ופסול הוא ומשפחתו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:9:1.english: [A challenge] over a family flaw - He is a slave — he comes from a family of a slave who was not emancipated — and he and his family are disqualified.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:9:2.hebrew: אמשפחה קמסהדי - ולאו משום האי לחודיה מסהדי, הלכך סהדותא אחרינא הוא, ולאו כנוגע בעדות דמי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 23b:9:2.english: They are testifying about the family - And they are not testifying on account of this [man] alone; therefore, it is another testimony, and [he] is not considered like [one who has] a conflict of interest in the testimony.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23b:11:1.hebrew: ורבנן סברי צריך לברר - ה"ג הקונטרס ללשון אחרון: "דרבנן סברי דצריך לברר כו'". אם יאמר אדם בב"ד: "אביא ב' כיתי עדים כשרים", צריך לברר דבריו ולהביא שתי כיתי עדים כשרים, ואם לא הביאם כשרים — יפסיד; הלכך אינו יכול לפסול הראשונים, שאם הראשוני' פסולים, זה לא יגבה חובו בעדים אחרונים, שצריך לברר ולהביא כולם כשרים. וקשה לר"ת, דבפ' גט פשוט (ב"ב קסט: ושם) משמע דאפילו מאן דאמר "צריך", היינו לכתחילה יאמרו לו ב"ד: "ברר דבריך", אבל מכל מקום אם אין יכול לברר — בכך לא יפסיד. ונראה לר"ת כפ"ה ללשון ראשון: ר"מ סבר צריך לברר, הלכך יכול לפסול הראשונים, לפי שלא יפסיד שום דבר אם הראשונים פסולין, לפי שבית דין אומרים לו: "ברר דבריך", דמסתמא יעשה מה שב"ד יצוה עליו, וא"כ לא יפסיד לפסול הראשונים, שמתקיים העדות בשאר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23b:11:1.english: "And the Rabbis hold that one is required to substantiate" - This is the reading of Rashi for the second version: "That the Rabbis hold that one is required to substantiate, etc." If a person says in court: "I will bring two sets of valid witnesses," he is required to substantiate his statement and bring two sets of valid witnesses, and if he does not bring them [all] valid, he loses [the case]. Therefore, [the opposing litigant] cannot disqualify the first [set], because if the first [witnesses] are disqualified, this [claimant] will not collect his debt through the latter witnesses, as he is required to substantiate [his claim] and bring all of them valid. And Rabbeinu Tam found this difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 169b and there), it implies that even the one who says "he is required [to substantiate]," that is only ab initio [that] the court says to him: "Substantiate your statement," but nevertheless, if he cannot substantiate [it], he does not lose [the case] on that account. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam [to explain] in accordance with Rashi's commentary for the first version: Rabbi Meir holds that he is required to substantiate; therefore, [the opposing litigant] can disqualify the first [witnesses], since [the claimant] will not lose anything if the first ones are disqualified, because the court says to him: "Substantiate your statement," for he will presumably do what the court commands him, and if so, he will not suffer a loss by [the other litigant] disqualifying the first [witnesses], as the testimony is established by the rest.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23b:1:1.hebrew: ואמר רב דימי כגון דקבליה בחד - תימה: למה לי לאתויי הא דרב דימי? ויש לומר: דאי לאו דרב דימי, לא הוה קשיא ליה "תנינא"; דאי מהתם, ה"א דמיירי דקביל עליה כבי תרי, דהוי תרתי לריעותא, והתם קאמר ר"מ דיכול לחזור, אבל בחדא לריעותא לא אמר רבי מאיר דיכול לחזור בו. ומשום הכי מייתי מילתיה דרב דימי, דקא משמע לן דאפילו בחדא ריעותא קאמר ר' מאיר יכול לחזור בו, וקא מקשי שפיר "תנינא":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 23b:1:1.english: "And Rav Dimi says: Such as where he accepted him as one" - [This is] puzzling: Why was it necessary [for the Gemara] to cite this [statement] of Rav Dimi? And one can say that were it not for [this statement] of Rav Dimi, it would not have raised the objection [from] "We have learned [in a mishna]"; for if [we understood the mishna only] from there, I would have said that it is dealing with [a case where] he accepted [the disqualified judge] upon himself as [equivalent to] two [judges], which constitutes two detriments, and [only] there does Rabbi Meir say that he can retract, but in [a case of only] one detriment, Rabbi Meir would not have said that he can retract. And because of this, [the Gemara] cites the statement of Rav Dimi, which teaches us that even with [only] one detriment Rabbi Meir says [that] he can retract; and [thus the Gemara] raises the objection [from] "We have learned [in a mishna]" well.
